text:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV=pg-s1 latency_spike_us-east-interzone > SLO (p99) — auto-pager: @oncall
Maya (SRE): seeing a sharp p99 jump across US-EAST -> US-WEST cross-zone traffic. p95 up ~3x and p99 up ~10x. Streaming tails are stalling.
Maya (SRE): metrics: p95 120ms -> 420ms, p99 250ms -> 2.9s. Streaming stall rate +14% in the last 6m.
Alex (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing traces and logs. // taking pager
Jules (SRE): confirmed, dashboards show DNS timeouts and TLS handshake spikes coincident with the p99 spike.
Tom (NetEng): any signs of packet loss or BGP flaps between AZs?
Priya (Infra): looking at NAT gateway metrics for the egress path between az-a and az-b. Seeing increased retransmits and NAT connection churn.
Maya (SRE): streaming app logs show repeated errors in the tail: "upstream: TLS handshake timeout" and "connection reset by peer".
Maya (SRE): sample app trace:
```
2026-03-14T22:14:06Z request_id=abc123 latency=0.456s stage=connect tls_handshake=2.4s
2026-03-14T22:14:07Z request_id=def456 latency=3.12s stage=stream stall=true
```
Tom (NetEng): running quick mtr between hosts in az-a -> az-b
Tom (NetEng): results show 0.3-1.2% packet loss on intermediate NAT hop and high latency on the egress gateway.
Tom (NetEng): also noticed repeated TLS connection resets from the egress appliance logs.
Priya (Infra): checking DNS resolvers — some NXDOMAIN spikes and increased latency to resolver pool 10.2.5.8.
Jules (SRE): could be correlated: if DNS delays + TLS handshake retries = tail blowups for streaming connections.
Alex (oncall): what's our customer impact? Which clients are affected?
Maya (SRE): affected: hosted API clients in US-EAST region, streaming endpoints most impacted; customers on Dedicated in same zones seeing increased tail latencies and a few 5xx for streaming sessions.
Alex (oncall): escalate to P1 and notify CS/Sales for impacted customers list. @Priya can you confirm which NAT pool is hot?
Priya (Infra): NAT pool nat-prod-eus-1 showing CPU spikes and conntrack table near limit. NAT instance id: i-0f9b7ea3
Priya (Infra): also seeing BGP neighbor resets with our transit provider around 22:11Z. Flap count +6 in 3m.
Tom (NetEng): hypothesis: transit provider had a routing change that pushed cross-AZ traffic through a congested/buggy NAT device -> TLS handshake spikes and packet loss -> streaming stalls.
Maya (SRE): mitigation options: 1) fail traffic to secondary NAT pool, 2) announce a more direct route to avoid transit path, 3) scale/replace NAT instance.
Alex (oncall): do we have a quick failover playbook for NAT? I want the fastest safe action to reduce customer impact.
Priya (Infra): playbook: flip egress route to nat-prod-eus-2 (secondary) and disable problematic NAT instance. Steps:
```
# promote secondary nat
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-0b2secondary
# drain i-0f9b7ea3
aws ssm start-session --target i-0f9b7ea3
# scale up conntrack
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
```
Tom (NetEng): before we flip, I'll sanity-check BGP status and confirm no other AZs will be impacted.
Maya (SRE): setting incident channel to #incidents and creating incident ticket. I'll push a mitigations banner on status.redwood.ai: "Investigating cross-zone latency spike affecting streaming; reduced performance for some US-EAST clients."
Maya (SRE): running a gradual failover: shifting 20% traffic to nat-prod-eus-2 now.
Jules (SRE): after 3m of 20% shift, p99 dropped from 2.9s -> 1.4s and streaming stall rate down ~6%.
Alex (oncall): nice. ramp to 60%.
Priya (Infra): ramped to 60%. conntrack usage on primary dropped; CPU still high but trending down.
Tom (NetEng): BGP neighbor with transit provider shows history of resets at 22:10-22:15Z. Reached out to provider engineer: @carrier-ops assigned ticket #CAR-4432.
Maya (SRE): p99 now 860ms, p95 160ms. Still above SLO but trending toward baseline.
Tom (NetEng): provider reported a partial egress path misconfiguration that caused packets to be hairpinned to an overloaded PE -> they've applied a rollback. Asking for validation.
Priya (Infra): started draining i-0f9b7ea3 and provisioning replacement NAT instance with newer AMI as a safety.
Alex (oncall): ok. what's next for customer comms and follow-ups?
Maya (SRE): action items:
- keep traffic on nat-prod-eus-2 for next 30m as stability buffer (Priya)
- collect packet captures + TLS handshake traces and upload to incident ticket (Tom)
- run a replay against streaming perf tests to validate tail latency (Jules)
- draft customer impact note for CS/Sales with list of affected customers (Maya)
- postmortem owner: Alex (oncall) unless someone volunteers for net/infra deep-dive

Tom (NetEng): uploading captures to s3://redwood-incidents/1774328150/captures.tar.gz
Jules (SRE): started synthetic replay, initial run shows tail latency normalized when using secondary NAT.
Maya (SRE): status page updated: "Mitigation in progress — traffic shifted to secondary egress; partial customer impact remains for streaming." :warning:
Alex (oncall): I'm going to hand off to night oncall @Maya at 23:00Z. Please ensure runbook and captures are attached to the ticket.
Maya (SRE): acknowledged, I'll own until stabilised and coordinate postmortem with NetEng/Infra.
Priya (Infra): replacing the problematic NAT instance now. New instance id i-0c9new will be up in ~4m.
deploy-bot: Deploy completed: nat-replace-job v1.2 -> success
Maya (SRE): final check: p99 at 310ms, p95 130ms after full failover + NAT replacement. Rolling back to primary not recommended until provider confirms route stability.
Alex (oncall): great work. creating incident doc and scheduling 1hr bridge for root-cause at 08:00Z tomorrow. Assigning postmortem to Alex + Tom + Priya + Maya + Jules.
Maya (SRE): closing pager for now, keeping channel open for updates. I'll post final impact summary once CS confirms affected customer list.
Jules (SRE): note: correlate ingress TLS retries in logs for further tuning of client retry/backoff.
Maya (SRE): thanks team. :heart:
